job.title: MSL Manager
job.description:
We're proud to partner with an innovative pharma group to recruit an experienced Medical Science Liaison Leader to oversee their team of MSLs across NSW and QLD.

Reporting into the Medical Affairs leadership team, you will lead, coach and develop a team of MSLs - driving field effectiveness, capability uplift, and a culture of collaboration, accountability and continuous improvement.
 

Key Responsibilities
 
    • Lead, mentor and develop a team of MSLs across NSW and Qld.
    • Build capability through coaching, development planning and field engagement.
    • Drive scientific excellence and high standards of stakeholder engagement.
    • Support onboarding, training and ongoing professional development.
    • Foster an inclusive, high-performing and collaborative team culture.
    • Partner closely with Medical, Commercial and Cross-Functional stakeholders to deliver strategic objectives.
   
This is a unique opportunity to step into a highly visible leadership role where you'll influence team performance, shape culture, and play a key part in the success of a growing Medical Affairs function.

About You
 
  • Previous MSL management experience within the pharmaceutical industry.
  • Proven ability to coach, mentor and develop high-performing teams.
  • Strong performance management and leadership skills.
  • Experience leading teams through growth and change.
  • Collaborative stakeholder manager with strong communication skills.
  • Comfortable operating in a fast-paced, highly accountable environment.
  
If you have proven MSL leadership experience and are passionate about developing people, building culture, and driving high performance, we would welcome a confidential discussion. 

Why Join?
 
    • Strong pipeline with multiple launches anticipated over coming years.
    • Strategic and highly regarded Medical Affairs function.
    • Genuine investment in leadership development and capability building.
    • Collaborative culture with excellent opportunities for career growth.
 
Apply Now 
Take the next step in your Medical Affairs leadership career with a global organisation committed to innovation, patient outcomes and the development of its people.

job.title: Medical Device Assessor
job.description:
Our client is the Australian Government regulatory authority for the safety, quality and efficacy of therapeutic goods. They evaluate and approve a range of prescription medicines, OTC and complementary medicines, and medical devices before they can be sold in Australia. 

About the Role 
We are looking for a biomedical engineer who has the ability to interpret and apply legislative guidelines and analyze technical information to make informed decisions and prepare high-quality regulatory decisions and notices to clients. 

Key Responsbilities
  • regulatory and technical assessment for medical devices including evaluating data, collating relevant expert advice and preparing clear evidence-based assessment outcomes and statements. 
  • Managing record keeping with the regulatory requirements
  • Providing clear advice and feedback on application assessment requirements and outcomes
About You
To be successful, you will need to be a qualified Biomedical or Mechanical Engineer with a bachelor's and/or master's degree. Ideally 12 months experience working in the medical device sector with some working knowledge of regulatory requirements for a range of devices - Class 1-111. Strong communication skills are essential, with strong technical writing and high attention to detail. This a team orientated environment where you will work closely with a range of stakeholders, and a sense of urgency will be required.

job.title: Principal Systems Engineer
job.description:
An exciting opportunity exists for an experienced Systems Engineer to join a growing Australian medical technology company developing innovative imaging and diagnostic platforms.

As the organisation transitions from advanced R&D into commercialisation and global regulatory approvals, this role will play a pivotal part in strengthening systems engineering capability, supporting FDA submissions, and ensuring products are developed in accordance with global medical device regulations.

This is a highly visible technical leadership position where you will work across software, electronics, optics, mechanical engineering, quality and regulatory functions to guide the development of sophisticated medical device systems from concept through to commercial deployment.

About the Role
Reporting to the CTO, you will provide Systems Engineering leadership across the organisation's product portfolio, ensuring robust engineering processes, regulatory compliance, and successful product integration. You will become a key technical authority responsible for driving requirements management, verification and validation activities, risk management, and system architecture decisions.

Key responsibilities include:
  • Leading systems engineering activities across the full product development lifecycle.
  • Defining and managing system requirements, architecture, interfaces, and traceability.
  • Driving verification and validation activities to ensure products meet customer, clinical and regulatory requirements.
  • Supporting FDA submissions and broader regulatory approval activities.
  • Ensuring compliance with relevant medical device standards, including IEC 62304, IEC 60601, ISO 14971 and ISO 13485.
  • Leading risk management activities throughout the product lifecycle.
  • Collaborating with Software, Electronics, Mechanical, Manufacturing, Quality and Regulatory teams to deliver integrated product solutions.
  • Providing technical leadership and mentoring engineers across multiple disciplines.
  • Driving continuous improvement initiatives across systems engineering processes and development methodologies.
  • Supporting strategic technology decisions for future product platforms and product enhancements.
  • Working closely with external development partners, suppliers and key technical stakeholders.
About You

To be considered for this role, you will have the following skills and qualifications:
  • A degree in Systems Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Software Engineering, Mechanical Engineering or a related discipline.
  • Significant experience developing complex products within the medical device industry and a strong understanding of Design Controls.
  • Strong knowledge of systems engineering principles, requirements management, verification and validation.
  • Experience with risk management frameworks and standards including ISO 14971.
  • Experience leading multidisciplinary engineering projects and influencing stakeholders at all levels.
  • Strong problem-solving, communication and stakeholder management skills.
  • An understanding of FDA regulatory requirements
This opportunity will suit a senior engineering professional who enjoys working at the intersection of technology, product development and regulatory compliance. This role is based 4 days per week in the office. For a confidential conversation about this role, please email gbitodi@onqrecruitment.com.au.

job.title: Medical Officer 3
job.description:
Are you an experienced Medical Practitioner (MBBS, AHPRA Registered) looking to apply your clinical expertise in a highly specialised regulatory environment?

Join a dedicated clinical evaluation team responsible for reviewing prescription medicines and providing evidence-based recommendations that support important regulatory decisions. Available on either a full-time or part-time basis (minimum three days per week), this role can be based in Sydney, Melbourne, Canberra or Brisbane and offers the opportunity to make a meaningful impact on public health outcomes across Australia.
  
As a Medical Officer, you will undertake critical assessments of clinical evidence submitted in support of prescription medicine applications. You will provide expert clinical and scientific advice, prepare comprehensive evaluation reports, and contribute to high-quality regulatory decision-making regarding the registration and variation of prescription medicines in Australia.

Key Responsibilities
  • Critically evaluate complex clinical and scientific data submitted as part of prescription medicine applications.
  • Prepare evidence-based assessments and recommendations to support regulatory decision-making.
  • Provide specialist medical and scientific advice on medicine safety, efficacy and quality.
  • Contribute to the timely delivery of prescription medicine evaluations while maintaining high regulatory standards.
  • Support organisational objectives through rigorous, transparent and defensible clinical assessments.
  • Collaborate with multidisciplinary stakeholders in a highly specialised scientific environment.
About You 
To be successful in this role, you will possess:
  • Medical qualification.Hold a qualification in Medicine and be registered as a medical practitioner with the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency.
  • Highly developed clinical knowledge and the ability to critically analyse complex clinical data.
  • Australian Citizenship.
Position Detail 
  • Employment Type: Full-time or Part-time (up to 37.5 hours per week)
  • Contract Duration: 12 months from commencement with potential extension
  • Locations: Canberra, Sydney (Parramatta), Brisbane or Melbourne
Please note that applications for this role will close at 10am on November 6th. For a confidential conversation about this role, please email Grace Bitodi at gbitodi@onqrecruitment.com.au.

job.title: Embedded Software Engineer
job.description:
An exciting opportunity exists for an experienced Embedded Software Engineer to join a growing Australian medical technology organisation that is transitioning from advanced R&D into commercialisation. This role offers the opportunity to contribute to the development of highly sophisticated medical devices that combine software, electronics, optics, mechanics, cybersecurity and advanced imaging technologies.

Working within a close-knit multidisciplinary engineering team, you will play a key role in designing, developing and maintaining embedded software for complex regulated products while helping build the foundations for future platform development.

About the Role
Reporting to the Chief Technology Officer, you will be responsible for the development and verification of embedded software across a suite of medical devices. You will work closely with systems, electronics, mechanical, quality, regulatory and manufacturing teams to ensure software is developed in accordance with regulatory and quality requirements. 

Key responsibilities include:
  • Designing, developing, verifying and maintaining embedded software in C/C++
  • Developing software for RTOS and embedded Linux environments
  • Supporting hardware-software integration, debugging and verification activities
  • Contributing to software architecture and design decisions
  • Producing high-quality technical and regulatory documentation
  • Supporting software verification and validation activities
  • Ensuring compliance with applicable medical device regulations and standards
  • Collaborating with cross-functional teams to support product development and commercialisation activities 
About You

To be successful in this position, you will bring:
  • Degree qualifications in Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Computer Science or a related discipline
  • Strong commercial experience in embedded software development
  • Advanced C/C++ programming skills
  • Experience with ARM-based microcontrollers
  • Strong RTOS experience, ideally FreeRTOS and/or Zephyr
  • Experience developing software for embedded Linux environments
  • Proven hardware-software integration and debugging capabilities
  • Understanding of communication protocols such as SPI, I2C, UART, CAN, USB and Ethernet
  • Excellent communication and documentation skills
  • Experience working within regulated industries such as medical devices, aerospace, defence, automotive or similar highly regulated environments 
Why Join?
  • Work on genuinely innovative medical technology with real-world impact
  • Join a business entering an exciting commercialisation and growth phase
  • Collaborate with experienced multidisciplinary engineers and technology leaders
  • Have significant influence on the future software architecture of next-generation products
  • Opportunity to grow your career within a business investing heavily in product development and innovation 
If you are passionate about embedded systems, enjoy solving complex technical challenges and would like to contribute to breakthrough medical technology, we would love to hear from you. For a confidential conversation, please email Grace Bitodi, gbitodi@onqrecruitment.com.au.

job.title: New Product Engineer
job.description:
Our client is an Australian based medical technology company developing innovative imaging technology with multiple clinical applications which enhances patient outcomes.
  
As a New Product Engineer in medical devices – we want to see your passion for delivering commercialized products that improve efficiencies and patient outcomes; we want to see your love for working cross functionally and your amazing problem-solving skills.
  
Opportunity
The purpose of this role is to assist with the design of new devices and the transfer of existing designs into production. The successful candidate, will be responsible for evaluating and selecting suppliers, developing safe and efficient manufacturing processes, preparing documentation, and performing process qualifications. The key focus will be modifying designs for Manufacture (DfX), and Design for Test (DFT), manufacturing transfer, and commercialization activities to enable products to move from development into production and then to market launch.
  
About You
You will hold a Bachelor’s degree as a mechanical engineer or mechatronic engineer with at least 2 years’ experience or more in medical devices or a highly regulated industry. You need to have hands-on manufacturing transfer skills, and a high level of proficiency in SolidWorks. You will need to be confident in assisting device design, risk management, prototyping, and verification and validation. Experience in DfM is essential, and DfA – design for assembly. You will have a process improvement mindset and be capable of doing root cause analysis and identifying solutions. Any regulatory and/or FDA knowledge will be highly regarded, and prior experience with ISO13485 and ISO9001 ideal. It is a cross functional role, and you will work closely with the engineering, production, and operational teams, so clear communication skills and technical writing skills are essential.
  
This is an exciting opportunity to work closely with an experienced team, where you can expect excellent career growth and the opportunity to add value and take responsibility for your own projects.

job.title: Principle Software Engineer - Medical Devices
job.description:
An exciting opportunity exists for an experienced Software Engineer to join a growing Australian medical technology company developing innovative imaging and diagnostic platforms. As the organisation transitions from advanced R&D into commercialisation and global regulatory approvals, this role will play a critical part in shaping the future of its software platforms and engineering capability. 

This is a hands-on leadership role where you will combine technical expertise, architectural decision-making, mentoring, and regulatory compliance knowledge to guide the development of complex medical device software systems. You will work closely with multidisciplinary engineering teams and external technology partners while helping drive the company's next-generation product platform.

About the Role

Reporting to the CTO, you will take ownership of software engineering across the entire product ecosystem, spanning embedded software, firmware, application software, cybersecurity considerations, and system integration. You will provide technical leadership to a growing software team while remaining actively involved in software design and development.
Key responsibilities include:
  • Leading software architecture decisions across embedded and application software platforms.
  • Designing and developing robust, scalable, and maintainable software solutions for regulated medical devices.
  • Driving software development activities across both new product development and existing product enhancement programs.
  • Ensuring compliance with medical device regulatory standards and software quality requirements.
  • Collaborating with Systems, Electronics, Mechanical, Manufacturing, Quality, Regulatory and Clinical teams.
  • Leading code reviews, technical reviews, software verification and validation activities.
  • Supporting regulatory submissions, audits, and compliance activities.
  • Identifying and implementing continuous improvements to software engineering processes, tools, and practices.
  • Contributing to strategic technology decisions for future product platforms. 
About You

To be considered for this role, you will have the following skills and qualifications:
  • A degree in Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Electronics Engineering or a related discipline.
  • 10+ years' experience developing software for medical devices.
  • Strong expertise in C/C++ software development.
  • Extensive experience with embedded systems, embedded Linux, RTOS environments and hardware-software integration.
  • A strong understanding of software architecture, systems integration, communications protocols and real-time systems.
  • Knowledge of IEC 62304, ISO 14971, ISO 13485 or comparable regulatory frameworks.
  • Experience leading software teams, mentoring engineers and driving technical excellence.
  • Experience with FPGA-based systems, ARM microcontrollers, 
  • Excellent stakeholder engagement and cross-functional communication skills. 
This opportunity will suit a senior professional who enjoys solving complex technical challenges whilst helping build products that can make a meaningful difference to patient outcomes. For a confidential conversation about the role, please contract Grace Bitodi at gbitodi@onqrecruitment.com.au.

job.title: APS5 HTA Support Officer

Working in a collaborative and fast-paced environment, you'll have the opportunity to contribute to meaningful outcomes that impact the Australian healthcare system.

About the Role

This role is ideal for candidates who enjoy stakeholder engagement, coordination and administration, and are looking to build experience within the health sector and broader government environment.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Preparing, reviewing and publishing documentation
  • Drafting meeting minutes and consultation summaries

  • Liaising with a broad range of internal and external stakeholders
  • Assisting with briefing materials, correspondence and scheduling activities

  • Excellent organisational and time management abilities
  • Experience providing administrative, project or secretariat support
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and relationship management skills

Highly regarded:
